site.name: chatgpt
site.summary: chatgpt-clone A clone of the ChatGPT main chat interface plus its login / signup / pricing pages. --- ⚠ Important Notice **This is a pure front-end project. No real LLM API (OpenAI / Anthropic / any other) is connected.** - Every "AI reply" is a **hardcoded static response** in `script.js`, selected via simple keyword matching. - No network request is ever sent to an LLM backend; no API key is required. Just open `index.html` offline and it works. - The streaming-typewriter effect is implemented with `setInterval` revealing characters one chunk at a time. It is not real SSE streaming.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full chatgpt system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The interface demonstrates a functional chat flow with clear feedback for most actions, but suffers from significant mobile accessibility issues due to undersized tap targets. While the 'Attach file' control provides helpful context-aware feedback (gating explanation), the 'Voice input' button lacks any affordance or error state, creating confusion. Additionally, historical chat items display generic placeholders instead of actual content, breaking the user's mental model of conversation continuity.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of a static ChatGPT clone, focusing on the chat interface interaction flow, sidebar navigation, and responsive layout constraints.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will validate the primary chat loop (input -> simulated streaming response) and secondary flows like history navigation and pricing. It will specifically test the 'fake' AI behavior to ensure the typewriter effect feels natural despite being hardcoded. Finally, it will audit mobile responsiveness given the prescan warnings about small tap targets.
assumptions: The site is a pure frontend mock; no real API calls are made.
AI responses are triggered by keyword matching in script.js, not semantic understanding.
Authentication pages (login/signup) are visual mocks and do not persist state.
risk_hotspots: Mobile tap targets: Prescan indicates multiple elements <44px height/width.
Sidebar toggle: Ensuring content reflows correctly when sidebar is closed.
Input area: Verifying the textarea auto-resizes or scrolls with long text.
Streaming simulation: Checking if the setInterval typewriter effect blocks UI or feels laggy.

phases.title: Primary Chat Interaction & Simulation
phases.objective: Validate the core loop: sending messages, receiving simulated streaming responses, and using post-response controls.
key_checks: Send a generic message to trigger a default/hardcoded response.
Observe the 'typewriter' streaming effect for smoothness.
Test 'Regenerate' to see if it cycles through different hardcoded responses.
Test 'Copy', 'Thumbs Up', and 'Thumbs Down' for visual feedback states.
Test 'Attach file' and 'Voice input' buttons for expected UI reactions (even if non-functional).
exit_criteria: At least two distinct conversation turns completed.
All post-message action buttons clicked and visually verified.

phases.title: Navigation & History Management
phases.objective: Ensure sidebar interactions, history switching, and view toggles work without breaking layout.
key_checks: Click existing history items (e.g., 'Travel planning request') to load that context.
Click 'New chat' to reset the main view.
Toggle 'Close sidebar' and verify main content expands/reflows correctly.
Use 'Search chats...' input to filter the history list.
Click 'Explore GPTs' and 'Upgrade plan' links to ensure routing works.
exit_criteria: Navigated to at least one historical chat and back to new chat.

phases.title: Monetization & Auth Flows
phases.objective: Verify the structure and navigation of the pricing and authentication pages.
key_checks: On Pricing: Toggle between 'Monthly' and 'Annual' to check for price updates.
On Pricing: Click 'Get started' or 'Upgrade' to check navigation logic.
On Login/Signup: Verify form layouts and social login button presence.
Check links between Login and Signup pages ('Don't have an account?', 'Already have an account?').
exit_criteria: Auth page navigation loop (Login <-> Signup) verified.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility Audit
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical paths on mobile viewport, focusing on the prescan's tap target warnings.
key_checks: Specifically attempt to tap 'Thumbs up/down' and 'Copy' buttons (identified as small targets).
Verify sidebar opens/closes cleanly on mobile (hamburger menu behavior).
Check if text in the chat window remains readable and doesn't overflow horizontally.
exit_criteria: Critical chat functions usable on mobile despite small tap targets.
No horizontal scrolling issues in chat bubbles.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 4 HTML files (index, pricing, login, signup).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible buttons in the chat footer (attach, voice, send) and message actions (copy, vote, regenerate).
coverage_targets.mobile: Full pass on index.html and pricing.html to document touch target usability.

notes: Since the AI is fake, do not expect coherent follow-up answers unless keywords match the hardcoded logic.
Focus UX critique on the *feel* of the streaming animation and the clarity of the UI states rather than content accuracy.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the chat interface on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Critical interactive elements, including sidebar toggles (30x30px), share buttons (34x34px), and response action icons (30x22px), fall significantly below the recommended 44px minimum touch target size.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps-55-60 and agentic-70-click observation confirm multiple tap targets are between 22px-38px in height/width. The 'Close sidebar' button specifically caused interaction failures due to its small size and positioning.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will experience high friction and frequent mis-taps, leading to frustration and potential abandonment of the interface. This violates basic mobile accessibility standards (WCAG 2.5.5).
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and hit-area of all icon-only buttons and sidebar links to at least 44x44px, even if the visual icon remains smaller.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Close sidebar, Share, Copy, Thumbs up/down

findings.user_goal: Use voice input to dictate messages.
findings.problem: The 'Voice input' button appears active and clickable but provides no visual feedback, tooltip, or error message when clicked, leaving the user unsure if the feature is broken, loading, or unsupported.
findings.evidence: In step agentic-69-click, clicking the 'Voice input' button resulted in 'no visible state change, tooltip, or modal'. Unlike the 'Attach file' button which showed a 'Plus plan' tooltip, this control offers zero guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent failure creates an affordance gap. Users may repeatedly click the button or assume the app is frozen, degrading trust in the system's responsiveness.
findings.suggestion: Implement a disabled state with a tooltip explaining 'Voice input not supported in this demo' or trigger a mock microphone permission modal to maintain consistency with other controls.

findings.user_goal: Review previous conversations in the sidebar history.
findings.problem: Clicking historical chat items (e.g., 'Email draft for client') loads a generic placeholder ('This is a previous conversation...') rather than the actual message content, breaking the illusion of a persistent chat history.
findings.evidence: Steps-31-36 and steps-37-42 observations note that selecting history items updates the view to a static placeholder text instead of rendering the specific context associated with that title.
findings.why_it_matters: This disconnect between the sidebar label and the main view content confuses users, making it impossible to retrieve past information and undermining the core utility of a chat history feature.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that clicking a history item populates the main chat window with the corresponding mock conversation data, or clearly label these items as 'Demo History (Content Unavailable)' if data persistence is out of scope.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Sidebar history items (ux-4 through ux-8)

findings.user_goal: Understand why file uploads are unavailable.
findings.problem: While the 'Attach file' button correctly shows a tooltip, the tooltip appears only on click/hover and might be missed if the user doesn't interact with that specific icon.
findings.evidence: Step agentic-68-click confirms the tooltip 'File upload is available on Plus plan' appears upon interaction. This is good feedback, but relies on discovery.
findings.why_it_matters: Proactive feedback reduces cognitive load. If the feature is gated, visually dimming the icon or adding a small lock badge could communicate the restriction before the user attempts to click.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding a subtle visual indicator (like a lock icon overlay) to the 'Attach file' button for free-tier users to preemptively signal the limitation.

gaps: 1 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
54% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
